---
title: "Speed"
subtitle: "tidyMacro against the reference MATLAB codes and against other R packages, same specifications"
editor: visual
number-sections: false
execute:
  # The charts and tables are read from speed_summary.csv and
  # speed_rpkgs_summary.csv, so re-execute on every render instead of keeping
  # a frozen copy.
  freeze: false
editor_options:
  chunk_output_type: console
---

```{r, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(gt)
library(gtExtras)
speed <- read.csv("speed_summary.csv", check.names = FALSE)
speed_r <- read.csv("speed_rpkgs_summary.csv", check.names = FALSE)
col_ml <- "#eb6834"
col_r <- "#2a78d6"

# Time of MATLAB (3 threads each) and of the R package (1 thread each)
# relative to tidyMacro = 1, log axis, ratios in two columns on the right.
labels <- c(chol = "Recursive bootstrap", bq = "Long-run bootstrap",
            mbb = "Proxy SVAR, block bootstrap", sign = "Sign restrictions",
            narr = "Sign and narrative", signiv = "Sign and instrument",
            msw = "Weak-instrument sets", lp = "Local projections",
            lpiv = "LP-IV", panel = "Panel LP")
cmp <- c("MATLAB (3 threads each)", "R package (1 thread each)")
ratio_fmt <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "fg", digits = 2)
both <- bind_rows(
  transmute(speed, routine, Type, Comparison = cmp[1], ratio = `Speed-up`,
            lab = ratio_fmt(`Speed-up`), xlab = 500),
  transmute(speed_r, routine, Type, Comparison = cmp[2], ratio = `Speed-up`,
            lab = paste0(ratio_fmt(`Speed-up`), " (", Package, ")"), xlab = 1700)
) |>
  mutate(Type = factor(Type, levels = c("Monte Carlo", "Deterministic")),
         Comparison = factor(Comparison, levels = cmp))
ord <- both |> group_by(routine) |> summarise(m = max(ratio))
both$Method <- factor(labels[both$routine],
                      levels = labels[ord$routine[order(ord$m)]])
hdr <- data.frame(Type = factor("Monte Carlo", levels = levels(both$Type)),
                  x = c(1, 500, 1700), lab = c("tidyMacro = 1", "MATLAB", "R package"),
                  hjust = c(0.5, 0, 0))

# Table of medians; ref_col is the reference timing column.
table_speed <- function(df, cols, ref_col, title, subtitle) {
  df |>
    arrange(factor(Type, levels = c("Monte Carlo", "Deterministic")), desc(`Speed-up`)) |>
    select(Type, all_of(cols), `Speed-up`) |>
    gt(groupname_col = "Type") |>
    gt_theme_nytimes() |>
    tab_header(title = title, subtitle = subtitle) |>
    fmt_number(columns = c(all_of(ref_col), `tidyMacro (s)`), n_sigfig = 3) |>
    fmt_number(columns = `Speed-up`, n_sigfig = 2, pattern = "{x}×") |>
    tab_style(style = cell_text(font = "monospace", size = px(13)),
              locations = cells_body(columns = any_of(c("tidyMacro function",
                                                        "Package function")))) |>
    tab_style(style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
              locations = cells_body(columns = `Speed-up`)) |>
    tab_style(style = cell_text(size = px(14), color = "#111111"),
              locations = cells_row_groups())
}
```

tidyMacro is timed twice: against the MATLAB code that each method on the [Validation](validation.qmd) page is compared with, and against the R packages that cover the same task. Both comparisons use the same data, lag orders, horizons and draw counts on each side.

- **Timing.** Wall-clock time of one complete call, including VAR estimation. Each routine is run once untimed as a warm-up. Monte Carlo routines are then timed `r max(speed$reps[speed$Type == "Monte Carlo"])` times with different seeds and deterministic routines `r max(speed$reps[speed$Type == "Deterministic"])` times. The reported figure is the median.
- **Machine.** Intel Core i5-7360U (2 cores, 4 threads), macOS 13.6, MATLAB R2025b, R 4.6.0 with the reference BLAS, tidyMacro 1.1.2.

```{r}
#| label: fig-speed
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5.4
#| fig-cap: "Time of the MATLAB reference codes (triangles, 3 threads each) and of other R packages (circles, 1 thread each) relative to tidyMacro, which is the line at 1, on a log axis. Values above 1 are slower than tidyMacro. The columns on the right give the ratios, with the R package in parentheses."
ggplot(both, aes(x = ratio, y = Method)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, colour = "#222222", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_line(aes(group = Method), colour = "grey80", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = Comparison, shape = Comparison), size = 3) +
  geom_text(aes(x = xlab, label = lab), hjust = 0, size = 3.6, colour = "#333333") +
  geom_text(data = hdr, aes(x = x, y = Inf, label = lab, hjust = hjust),
            vjust = -0.8, size = 3.6, fontface = "bold", colour = "#222222",
            inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200),
                labels = c("0.5", "1", "2", "5", "10", "20", "50", "100", "200"),
                expand = c(0, 0)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.5, 9000), clip = "off") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(col_ml, col_r), name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(17, 16), name = NULL) +
  facet_grid(Type ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y") +
  labs(x = "Time relative to tidyMacro", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", legend.justification = "left",
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = "grey90", linewidth = 0.3),
        strip.placement = "outside",
        strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 90, face = "bold"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(colour = "#222222"),
        plot.margin = margin(16, 5.5, 5.5, 5.5))
```

## Against the MATLAB reference codes

- **Thread budget.** Both sides get 3 threads. tidyMacro receives `n_threads = 3`; MATLAB runs under `maxNumCompThreads(3)`. The reference MATLAB codes have no `parfor` loops, so in MATLAB the budget only reaches multithreaded linear algebra.
- **Sign + external IV.** The full Cesa-Bianchi and Sokol (2022) specification takes hours in the VAR Toolbox, so a lighter version is timed: one instrument (the monetary-policy surprise) instead of two, and the financial-shock signs imposed on impact only.
- **LP-DiD** is not timed, because its reference is Stata output.

```{r}
#| label: speed-table
table_speed(speed,
            c("Method", "Data", "Workload", "tidyMacro function", "MATLAB (s)",
              "tidyMacro (s)"),
            "MATLAB (s)",
            title = "Median seconds per call",
            subtitle = "Same data and specification on both sides; 3 threads each")
```

## Against other R packages

- **Packages.** [vars](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=vars) for bootstrapped recursive and long-run responses, [VARsignR](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=VARsignR) for sign restrictions, and [lpirfs](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=lpirfs) for local projections. VARsignR is archived on CRAN; version 0.1.3 is installed from the archive.
- **Thread budget.** These packages run on one thread, so tidyMacro gets `n_threads = 1` as well.
- **Same estimates.** Before timing, the script checks that each pair estimates the same model: the VAR coefficients of tidyMacro and vars agree, and the point responses of tidyMacro and lpirfs agree to machine precision. vars resamples residuals, so tidyMacro uses its residual bootstrap here. lpirfs projects every endogenous variable on the shock and on lags of all of them, so the tidyMacro calls use the same outcomes and regressors.
- **Sign restrictions.** Both sides return 1,000 accepted draws with the signs imposed over horizons 0 to 5, VARsignR with the 200 × 200 draw budget of its documentation. `uhlig.reject()` can keep several accepted rotations from one posterior draw, while `fSignRestr()` keeps one per posterior draw, so VARsignR needs far fewer posterior draws for the same 1,000.

```{r}
#| label: speed-rpkgs-table
table_speed(speed_r,
            c("Method", "Data", "Workload", "tidyMacro function", "Package",
              "Package function", "Package (s)", "tidyMacro (s)"),
            "Package (s)",
            title = "Median seconds per call",
            subtitle = "Same data and specification on both sides; one thread each")
```
